title: Function‑Based Views
description: Write simple views that handle HTTP requests and return HTTP responses.

slides.title: A Simple View
Anatomy of a View 🧩
slides.content:
A function‑based view always takes a **request** object as its first parameter. It can do anything, but must return an **HttpResponse** (or raise an exception).

You can also use **shortcuts** like `render()` to return HTML templates.

slides.title: Using Templates
slides.content: Instead of writing HTML in Python, use the `render` shortcut:

quizData.question: What must a Django view always return?
quizData.explanation: The view must return an `HttpResponse` or an exception; otherwise Django will raise an error.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Keep views thin

Views should contain only request/response logic. Move business logic to models or separate utility functions.
